#  A round owes a pass-2 review of its own diff.  R6 and R7 both shipped without one --
#  the second time one round after the first was caught, written down and corrected --
#  which is why this is a tracked file checked mechanically rather than a habit.
#  A receipt says a review was CONVENED and recorded against the commit it reviewed.
#  It says NOTHING about whether the review was any good; nothing mechanical can.

#  old single column was green for any value of the question that matters, which is the

Four seats SOUND (agy, deepseek, minimax, and grok on the arithmetic); glm DEFECTIVE and it was RIGHT TWICE AND WRONG ONCE, all three worth recording. WRONG: its "a 4 KB write touches at most TWO pages, so 2 translations not 4" assumed a 4096-byte granule; the split granule is 1024 (MRW_SPLIT_MASK 0x3ff), so 4096/1024 = 4 chunks and the figure stands. RIGHT (1): my parenthetical "(the PAGE split)" is what INVITED that misreading -- the label contradicted the granule in the very comment written to stop that conflation. Relabelled to name the 1024-byte SPLIT granule explicitly. RIGHT (2): the block carried PROCESS NARRATIVE -- "a measuring seat walked the offsets", "corrected 2026-08-20", "ONE mis-derived constant became two records defects" -- which belongs in this receipt and the ledger, not in memory_rw.c. Project ethos is terse portable C99 and minimal surgical changes; a maintainer needs the number and why it is right, not how it was found. Trimmed. Also acted on its point 4 (grep the file for surviving 256/4KB claims): line 72 already warns the real page is 8 KB, so the corrected block now says so rather than leaving a bare "4 KB page" to be misread. glm declined to verify the two MEASURED claims from the packet and said "I cannot tell from this packet" rather than guessing -- the honest form. column6: SHIP-WITH-FIX, and the fix is handed to the in-flight pitflip round to avoid contending for the same file. SIX SEATS SOUND, CODEX DEFECTIVE -- and codex was RIGHT: "the latch is never consumed, so the selected counter returns zero indefinitely." VERIFIED IN SOURCE: latched[] is SET at :212, cleared ONLY at :219 by a non-latch mode write, and NEVER cleared by the read at :163. So after one latch command every subsequent read of that counter returns 0 until the guest happens to rewrite the mode byte. A real 8254 CONSUMES the latch per the programmed RW format. NOT a regression -- pre-#439 a latch clobbered mode_byte and subsequent reads also fell to the default arm returning 0, plus an unsilenceable flood -- but a real defect in the fix, found by the one seat that had been walled for the pass-1 panel. glm gestured at the same thing ("the sticky latch"). THE CONSUME SEMANTICS INTERACT WITH THE LSB/MSB FLIP-FLOP: in 16-bit mode a real latch delivers TWO bytes before reverting, which is precisely the selector pitflip is fixing -- so the fix belongs in that round, with a named detector row that latches, reads twice, and asserts the second read is not still 0. The six SOUND verdicts converged on the substantive question the brief asked -- agy: "returning 0 avoids guest kernel divide-by-zero crashes, preserves programmed mode state"; deepseek: "the least harmful of three wrong answers and not a guest-visible regression"; minimax: "the write-side fix matches the 8254 and removes a real bug". So the refusal of the pass-1 majority is VINDICATED by pass 2, and the shipped shape stands; what was missed was the consume.

This receipt is that missing review. ***  Eight seats fired: 7/7 scriptable answered plus the opus5 measuring seat; fable5 DELIBERATELY NOT FIRED per the owner's standing deprioritisation, recorded as a deliberate omission and never as agreement. THE FINDING: of the three mechanisms #440 adds, the CONTROL-WORD REWIND SHIPPED WITH ZERO COVERAGE. Deleting one line -- d->wr_msb[d->counter_select] = 0; -- passed ALL TEN rows while measurably corrupting the datasheet's own convention-1 sequence (Control Word, write LSB, Control Word, write LSB, write MSB): readback 0x1140 instead of 0x4011, and the guest given 265 Hz where it asked for 73. TWO SEATS FOUND IT INDEPENDENTLY -- opus5 by building eight binaries, codex by reading alone. A sibling mutant (literal 0 for the counter index in the rewind) also passed all ten and broke every counter but 0. Closed by arms W/X and rows R10/R11; R11 is NOT redundant with R10 -- it is the only row that sees the sibling (MUT-D: R10 ok, R11 FAIL). THE FIRST KILL TEST WAS A VOID CONTROL THAT SCORED ITSELF GREEN: run through wsl -- bash -c from git-bash, the shell ate $M, no mutant was ever applied, and both rows printed ok on unmodified source; 'cp: cannot stat' was the only symptom and it did not stop them printing. Re-run from a script file on disk, per the documented fix. TWO WRONG RECORDS corrected in the source: the comment claiming '#439's measured behaviour is unchanged' is MEASURED FALSE (two toggles preserve the STARTING phase, so an even-parity gettick() is a no-op, but at ODD parity the first read consumes the latch and the second returns the live LSB -- 0x9c00, not 0x0000); and the struct comment read as though the datasheet describes read/write flip-flops, which it does not -- the phrase never appears in the local i8254.txt, whose only flip-flop hits are the GATE edge detector, so two flip-flops is now stated as the inference from an observable sequence that it is. CODEX DISSENTED, DO NOT SHIP, on two grounds, both settled by looking rather than by count. (1) mode_byte is still GLOBAL so per-counter flip-flops sit under a shared format byte -- REAL, and it IS pitclobber, measured IDENTICAL on HEAD and #440 and therefore pre-existing; barred from this round by the reopening rule, and it now carries a witness it lacked this morning (the standard PC PIT init returns 0x9c9c, the low byte twice). (2) Consuming the latch after ONE post-latch read contradicts p.8's 'two bytes must be read' -- a GENUINE OPEN QUESTION: the measuring seat reached the same fact and the opposite reading, and BOTH agree the local text does not say whether a latch rewinds the read flip-flop. Filed as pitlatch2 as an honest UNKNOWN rather than resolved 7-1. KIMI's out-of-bounds finding (SC=11 indexing latched[3]/rd_msb[3]/wr_msb[3]) is REFUTED BY THE FILE: dev_8253.c:269-272 clamps counter_select > 2 back to 0, four lines above the first array write, so the premise cannot occur -- settled in under a minute. RESIDUAL the measuring seat named and I did not fix: R4/R7/R8/R9 catch the READ-side rewind mutant only because PROLOGUE's A1 signature read leaves rd_msb[0] at 1, which nothing in the file states -- a PROLOGUE refactor silently un-pins it. column6: SHIP-WITH-CHANGES, applied in the same commit. *** SEVEN OF EIGHT SEATS SAID SHIP, AND THE 9-ROW DETECTOR THEY WERE APPROVING PASSED SIX MUTANTS. ***  The single dissent was the one seat that COMPILED AND RAN, and the sharpest of its six puts exit(1) BACK on a guest-reachable path -- the round's headline property -- with every row green: 'if (partial && writeflag == MEM_READ) exit(1);', measured to end the process on one mov.b. Root cause structural, not careless: reachable shapes are (read|write) x len(1|2|4) = SIX and the detector exercised FIVE -- no row did a 1-byte READ. Two more (delete BCR2's mask, add one to BCR3) escaped because BOTH write oracles were MASK-TRANSPARENT -- D1 wrote 0x89ab3ffd and 0x3ffd & 0x3ffd is 0x3ffd, so a row NAMED 'masked' could not see the mask. One constant (0xc003 -> 0x0001) kills both. A fourth neutered the whole big-endian lane, a fifth swapped the Ignored/Servicing ternary so the diagnostic stated the opposite of what happened. Detector 9 -> 13 rows; pre-fix 2/13; every mutant now killed by a named row; clean tree 13/13. *** THE READING SEATS EARNED THEIR PLACE ON THE SAME QUESTION: agy INDEPENDENTLY FOUND THE BIG-ENDIAN MUTANT BY READING ALONE (replace sh4_bsc16_shift's body with 'return 0;'), and codex reached the same requirement -- 'cover the big-endian 4-byte lane behavior; the code itself does not need a functional change.' ***  Reading seat named the family, measuring seat proved the instance. Codex also named a residual nobody else did: the latch keys on SITE, so a byte read can demote a later 4-byte write's first report -- consistent with the stated policy, so recorded not fixed. FOUR OF THE ROUND'S OWN ERRORS WERE CAUGHT BY RUNS, NOT REASONING: (1) the first version of the fix WAS mutant M1 -- the helper returned 1 unconditionally so a 1-byte write overwrote the whole register with 0xa5, and D3 caught it, a row a pass-1 seat had written against exactly that; (2) D4's first version ran the two sites in SEPARATE PROCESSES, so the shared-latch mutant passed 9/9 -- each fresh process starts with both flags clear, and the file's own docstring said 'in ONE process' while the code did not; (3) MY POSITIVE CONTROL PASSED 12/12, and assuming a dead pipeline would have buried a real hole -- neutering the len==2 fast path makes every LEGAL 16-bit driver access emit a complaint -q cannot silence, now pinned by D10, and five other mutants died in the same run so the pipeline was demonstrably alive; (4) D7b's expected constant was lifted from another probe with a different input, and its first input discriminated by one bit. TWO WRONG RECORDS IN MY OWN COMMENTS, measured false by the pass-2 seat: the len<2 guard's comment shouted that a 1-byte store is 'reachable -- measured' when the store is reachable but the FUNCTION is not reached with it (traced across all twelve report-calls); and the header comment argued against dropping a write while the code dropped one, invisibly so free-running because debug() computes v = verbose - 1 = -1 and returns. Both corrected to say what the code does. A FACTUAL ERROR IN MY PASS-1 BRIEF gave the cleanest test of the seat-class doctrine this project has: I asserted BCR3 is at 0xff800006 without opening sh4_bscreg.h:70, where it reads 0xff800050. EVERY SEAT THAT COULD OPEN THE HEADER CAUGHT IT (agy, kimi, grok); EVERY PACKET-FED SEAT BUILT ON IT, two producing whole designs around the imagined adjacency. Codex could have opened it and did not -- 'cannot check' and 'did not check' are different failures. Gate 6 EXPECT_CONVERTED 18 -> 19, and the first fix for that was wrong too: the probe named its send() local 'mark' rather than '_mark', so the guard was PRESENT but invisible to a census keying on the exact spelling, and my first comment blamed the census. '_mark' is the idiom in every other pty probe. Filed as sh4markspell. Gates: gate_hygiene PASS (48), gate_offline PASS (259), each run singly. Four trees byte-identical by cmp after the mutation runs; build/.MUTANT cleared only after that cmp against the REPO SOURCE passed.
